study: Bleses et al. 2021 (SPELL base arm, Grade-2 follow-up, PLoS ONE 16(10))
eval_evidence: The SPELL intervention was developed AND evaluated by the authors' research group (Aarhus University: Bleses, Dale; Justice an early-literacy intervention developer); 'researchers have developed and evaluated for efficacy.' Developer-conducted (despite the 'no competing interests' boilerplate).
developer_evidence: SPELL is delivered to children by the regular preschool teachers, who attended a short two-day teacher PD course; teachers (not developers) implement the curriculum in their own classrooms.
cascade_evidence: The publication does not specify who delivered the two-day teacher PD course (developers vs. trained intermediaries); registry codes the trainer as 'External' but the report itself is silent on the number of transmission hops.
counterfactual_evidence: Random assignment to SPELL vs. business-as-usual (BAU); BAU centers continued usual practice.
coaching_evidence: Base SPELL arm = a short two-day teacher PD course only, no ongoing in-class coaching (registry coaching=0). (The separate SPELL+PD arm adds 14 hours of extended PD, but that is not the registry-matched base arm.)
student_dose_evidence: SPELL is a 20-week storybook curriculum supplement delivered by teachers as 'two lessons weekly to children in small groups of about 4-6 children' (40 small-group lessons) -- a substantial added student-facing instructional dose beyond regular ECE.
maturity_evidence: SPELL is a one-time 20-week preschool delivery (single implementation, teachers new to it); no maturity axis. (The extracted outcome is the Grade-2 long-term follow-up of that single delivery.)
